sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Python is a high-level, readable language created by Guido van Rossum in 1991. It uses indentation instead of braces and focuses on clear syntax, making it one of the most popular first languages worldwide.
sections.examples:
# Python runs scripts, web apps, and notebooks
print("Welcome to Python")

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Python is used for web backends (Django, Flask, FastAPI), data science and AI, automation, scripting, and scientific computing.
sections.examples:
# Common roles Python fills today:
# - REST APIs and microservices
# - Machine learning pipelines
# - Data cleaning and dashboards

sections.title: Variables and types
sections.body: Variables store values. Python figures out the type from what you assign.
sections.examples:
name = "Alex"
age = 25
is_student = True
price = 19.99
print(name, age, type(price))

sections.title: Lists, tuples, and loops
sections.body: Lists are mutable sequences; tuples are fixed. for and while iterate over data.
sections.examples:
scores = [88, 92, 79]
scores.append(95)

for score in scores:
    print(score)

point = (10, 20)  # tuple — coordinates

sections.title: Dictionaries and sets
sections.body: Dicts map keys to values. Sets store unique items and support fast membership checks.

sections.title: Functions
sections.body: def creates reusable code. return sends a value back. Default parameters and type hints improve clarity.
sections.examples:
def greet(person: str, excited: bool = False) -> str:
    suffix = "!" if excited else "."
    return f"Hello, {person}{suffix}"

print(greet("Alex", excited=True))

sections.title: Conditionals and comprehensions
sections.body: if/elif/else branch logic. List comprehensions build lists in one expressive line.
sections.examples:
status = "adult" if age >= 18 else "minor"

squares = [n * n for n in range(1, 6)]
evens = [n for n in range(10) if n % 2 == 0]

sections.title: Modules and virtual environments
sections.body: Import modules to reuse code. pip installs packages; venv isolates project dependencies.
sections.examples:
import math
from datetime import date

print(math.sqrt(16))
print(date.today())

# Terminal:
# python -m venv .venv
# pip install requests

sections.title: Classes and OOP basics
sections.body: class groups data and behavior. __init__ initializes instances; methods define behavior.

sections.title: Files and error handling
sections.body: with open(...) safely reads and writes files. try/except catches runtime errors gracefully.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: JavaScript is the language of the web browser. Created in 1995, it adds interactivity to pages and, with Node.js, also powers servers and tools.
sections.examples:
// JavaScript runs in every major browser
console.log("Welcome to JavaScript");

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Front-end UIs use React, Vue, and Angular. Node.js builds APIs, real-time chat servers, and CLI tools.

sections.title: Variables
sections.body: Use let for values that change and const for values that should not be reassigned.

sections.title: Async with promises
sections.body: async functions return promises. await pauses until a promise settles.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Java is a statically typed language released in 1995. Its motto Write Once, Run Anywhere comes from the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Java powers enterprise backends, Android apps, banking systems, and big-data tools like Hadoop and Kafka.

sections.title: Classes and main
sections.body: Java is statically typed. Code lives in classes. The JVM starts at the main method.

sections.title: Methods and parameters
sections.body: Methods encapsulate behavior. Overloading allows same name with different parameter lists.

sections.title: Collections
sections.body: ArrayList stores a growable list. HashMap maps keys to values. Generics add type safety.

sections.title: Object-oriented programming
sections.body: Fields hold state; methods define behavior. private hides details; public exposes an API.

sections.title: Inheritance and interfaces
sections.body: extends inherits from a parent class. implements defines a contract multiple classes can share.

sections.title: Exception handling
sections.body: try/catch handles runtime errors. finally runs cleanup. throw creates custom failure paths.

sections.title: Streams and lambdas
sections.body: Java 8+ streams process collections declaratively. Lambdas shorten anonymous behavior.

sections.title: Build tools and projects
sections.body: Maven and Gradle manage dependencies and build lifecycle. Spring Boot accelerates REST APIs.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: C++ extends C with classes, templates, and the Standard Template Library (STL). It is compiled directly to fast native machine code.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: C++ is chosen when performance matters: game engines, operating systems, browsers, embedded devices, and trading systems.

sections.title: Types and output
sections.body: C++ requires explicit types. std::cout sends text to the console.

sections.title: Vectors
sections.body: std::vector is a dynamic array from the standard library.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Kotlin is a modern JVM language from JetBrains (2011). It is concise, null-safe, and fully interoperable with Java — the official language for Android app development.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Kotlin powers Android apps, server-side APIs (Ktor, Spring), multiplatform projects (KMP), and Gradle build scripts.

sections.title: val and var
sections.body: val is read-only; var can change. Types are inferred when obvious.
sections.examples:
fun main() {
  val name = "Alex"
  var age = 25
  val isStudent = true
  age += 1
  println("$name is $age years old")
}

sections.title: Functions and expressions
sections.body: fun declares functions. if/when are expressions that return values — less boilerplate than Java.

sections.title: Conditionals and loops
sections.body: Ranges like 1..5 include both ends. for iterates collections and ranges cleanly.
sections.examples:
val status = if (age >= 18) "adult" else "minor"
var total = 0
for (n in 1..5) total += n

val evens = (1..10).filter { it % 2 == 0 }

sections.title: Null safety
sections.body: ?. safely calls on nullable values. ?: supplies a default. !! forces non-null (avoid in production).
sections.examples:
val nickname: String? = null
val display = nickname ?: name
val length = nickname?.length ?: 0
println(display)

sections.title: Collections
sections.body: listOf and mapOf create immutable collections. mutableListOf and mutableMapOf allow changes.
sections.examples:
val tags = listOf("kotlin", "android")
val scores = mapOf("quiz" to 92, "lab" to 88)

val mutable = mutableListOf(1, 2, 3)
mutable.add(4)

sections.title: Data classes
sections.body: data class auto-generates equals, hashCode, copy, and component functions.
sections.examples:
data class Student(val name: String, val age: Int)

val student = Student(name, age)
val older = student.copy(age = age + 1)
println("${student.name} -> ${older.age}")

sections.title: Extension functions
sections.body: Add functions to existing types without inheritance — common in Kotlin standard library style.
sections.examples:
fun String.firstWord(): String =
  trim().substringBefore(' ')

println("Hello Kotlin".firstWord())  // Hello

sections.title: Coroutines overview
sections.body: suspend functions perform async work without blocking threads. launch and async structure concurrent tasks.

sections.title: Document structure
sections.body: HTML describes page structure. head holds metadata; body holds visible content.
sections.examples: Hello, Alex!

sections.title: CSS styling
sections.body: CSS controls appearance. Selectors target elements, classes, or IDs.
sections.examples:
body { font-family: sans-serif; margin: 2rem; }
.card { padding: 1rem; border: 1px solid #ccc; }

sections.title: Forms and inputs
sections.body: Forms collect user input. label improves accessibility.
sections.examples:
<form class="card">
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" type="email" required>
</form>

sections.title: Flexbox layout
sections.body: Flexbox arranges items in a row or column with gap and alignment properties.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: SQL is the standard language for talking to relational databases. You describe what data you want; the engine decides how to fetch it.
sections.examples:
-- SQL reads and writes rows in tables.
SELECT 'Welcome to SQL' AS message;

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Every major app stores structured data in PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, or SQLite.
sections.examples:
-- Common roles:
-- User profiles and authentication
-- E-commerce orders
-- Analytics reports

sections.title: Create a table
sections.body: Tables store rows of data. PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies a row.

sections.title: Joins
sections.body: JOIN combines rows from two tables using a related column.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Client/server architecture splits work between two roles: the client requests services and the server provides them over a network.
sections.examples:
Client (browser or app)
    |  HTTP request
    v
Server (API + database)
    |  HTTP response
    v
Client renders the result

sections.title: Frontend and backend
sections.body: The frontend is what users see and interact with. The backend handles business logic, authentication, and data storage.
sections.examples:
Frontend: React page, Android app screen
Backend: REST API, database, auth service
Communication: HTTP + JSON

sections.title: Real-life projects
sections.body: Every major web and mobile product uses this pattern at scale.
sections.examples:
Instagram app (client) -> Meta servers (backend)
Chrome (client) -> search and sync APIs
Uber app -> trip matching and payment servers

sections.title: Request and response
sections.body: A typical API call sends a method, headers, and optional body. The server returns a status code and data payload.
sections.examples:
GET /api/users/48291
Authorization: Bearer <token>

Response 200:
{ "username": "48291", "status": "active" }
